snippet.description:
Someone else can make you squirm with one touch, but try tickling yourself, and nothing happens. Why? Investigator Konstantina Kilteni went looking for answers and found something surprising. Socrates, Aristotle, Galileo, and Darwin all wondered about tickling, but there’s very little actual research on it. Two millennia later, we still don’t know what ticklishness is for. 

This week on Unexplainable, Noam Hassenfeld asks Konstantina what’s going on in our brains when we get tickled. Watch the full episode on Netflix or listen wherever you get your podcasts.

snippet.description:
Struggling to manage the vast UPSC syllabus with limited time? In this video, discover 7 scientific time management techniques for UPSC preparation to help you study smarter, prioritise effectively, and retain more.

Register for AIR 170 Webinar: https://shorturl.at/WOFT9

Apply for Rs.50,000 Scholarship for GS Foundation 2028: https://www.levelupias.com/scholarship-test-for-upsc-gs-foundation/

GS Foundation 2028: https://www.levelupias.com/courses/upsc-cse-gs-foundation-course/

Learn practical, research-backed strategies to structure your study schedule, make better use of your productive hours, minimise distractions, and revise consistently.

In this video, you’ll learn:
- How to plan your UPSC preparation backwards from your target exam
- How to prioritise tasks using the Eisenhower Matrix
- How to align your study schedule with your productivity rhythm
- How to use the Pomodoro technique for focused study sessions
- How to improve retention through spaced revision and interleaving
- How to reduce distractions and manage your study environment
- How to track mistakes and doubts with an Error Anatomy Ledger

Whether you’re a working professional, college student, or full-time UPSC aspirant, these techniques can help you make your study hours more productive and build a structured preparation strategy for UPSC CSE.
